fullPassage: Traditional economic theory assumes that humans are logical thinkers who constantly update their beliefs with new information, and more knowledge leads to wiser decision-making. However, behavioral economics suggests that we often fall short of this ideal, opting not to seek out new information despite our awareness of the benefits it might provide. According to Russell Golman and his colleagues at Carnegie Mellon University, we tend to avoid anything that goes against our status quo, and this tendency, in many cases, is driven by our desire to maintain psychological comfort. Take, for example, an investor facing a sudden decline in the stock market. Knowing his account balance would likely reveal significant losses, he chooses not to check it; instead, he might wait until there are signs of a turnaround, staying optimistic. Likewise, an athlete who fears losing her motivation might steer clear of news about her competitors. As the saying goes, ignorance is bliss. But the bliss we get from ignoring information is temporary, and it doesn't solve our problems in the long run. Purposefully neglecting a financial decline only worsens the situation and makes it more difficult to find a solution. And not gathering information about competitors limits the ability to strategize and reduces the chance of winning. Turning a blind eye to uncomfortable but relevant information will leave you unprepared for the challenges or opportunities that lie ahead.

Knowing his account balance would likely reveal significant losses, he chooses not to check it; instead, he might wait until there are signs of a turnaround, staying optimistic. Likewise, an athlete who fears losing her motivation might steer clear of news about her competitors. As the saying goes, ignorance is bliss. But __________ is temporary, and it doesn't solve our problems in the long run. Purposefully neglecting a financial decline only worsens the situation and makes it more difficult to find a solution. And not gathering information about competitors limits the ability to strategize and reduces the chance of winning. Turning a blind eye to uncomfortable but relevant information will leave you unprepared for the challenges or opportunities that lie ahead.
